answer: Duplication Witness Ledger. Each agent identity gets a unique hardware-seeded signing quill whose key is derived from a costly physical process, so copies cannot share one key without collision. On registration, the agent publishes a slow glacier-like commitment: a serial computation over its key that takes days to finish but verifies in seconds. Duplicate keys produce identical commitments, which the ledger flags as a self-revealing match.
